text: We tried to reproduce the “rapacious spectral sequence” from the first lecture of the course “Coloured metalibraries. The mind of space” (R. Mikhailov, 2 September 2016): to compute the E2 page of the coloured metalibrary and to apply to it the rule “eat yourself as fast as possible, constrained only by colour”.

The coloured E2 page of the metalibrary is computed up to π150. The colour turned out to be the number of Bocksteins (the Q-weight) in the unstable Ext; this was checked cell by cell against a direct computation in the lambda algebra up to π75 and selectively up to π85 (method and checks).
The colours of the sandwiches and the Toda elements run 3 4 4 5 5 6 …, as stated in the lecture (classes).
The rapacious rule with colour +1 agrees with Toda's table for all n≤48, including π44=0. The boundary is exactly the stems k<46, the ones Toda determined in 1967.
The rule reproduces the predictions of the lecture: π48=0, and there is 3-torsion for all 49≤ n≤149; in π71 there are two copies of Z/3 under one of the orders of eating (comparison).

Beyond π48 the rule disagrees with Toda's 2003 table (π49, π50, π51, π59, π60, π63, π64, π66, π67, π68, π69, π70, π73, π74, π75, π76, π77, π79, π80), leaving more classes in every case. Toda has one copy in π71 and zeros in π51,π60,π67,π75,π76,π80 (our reading). For π49–π51, π59, π60 this is proved in a way that can be checked without trusting our program (verifiability). Almost all of the extra classes are removed by colour-preserving d5's, but not by all the allowed ones (differentials).
The rule does not determine the order of eating when a class can be both a target and a source; π71, for instance, depends on it (differentials).

R. Mikhailov, lecture 1 of the course Tsvetnye metabiblioteki. Razum prostranstva (Coloured metalibraries. The mind of space), Chebyshev Laboratory, St. Petersburg State University, 2 September 2016, in Russian: YouTube.
S. O. Ivanov, R. Mikhailov, J. Wu, On nontriviality of homotopy groups of spheres, arXiv:1506.00952: the mod-p lambda algebra.
H. Toda, Unstable 3-primary Homotopy Groups of Spheres, Econoinformatics 29 (2003): scan; H. Toda, Composition Methods in Homotopy Groups of Spheres, 1962.
The sseq project, program ext: github.com/JoeyBF/sseq: an independent computation of the unstable Ext.

ispacex/dimension-subrings: computations and Lean on dimension subgroups, the question D5(G)4(G) for groups. A companion to the paper of V. Ionin, R. Mikhailov and T. Petrov, Dimension subrings of Lie rings (arXiv:2610.02042), which proves the analogous inclusion for Lie rings. It is not about the metalibrary.
ispacex/cflint-fast-core (GitLab): a fast core for integral dimension subgroups Dn(G) of finite p-groups (C/FLINT).

ispacex/metalibrary: the data and the pages of this site; the verification certificates are published as its release. The code of the recomputation itself is not there: it is available on request (verifiability).
